target_customer: HR and people operations teams at companies with remote workers
problem: Remote teams lacked engaging shared experiences during the pandemic.
business_model: Per event fees for managed virtual team experiences (per a third party archive page, unverified)

founders.name: John Friel
founders.background_notes: Listed by the YC page, which shows team size 2 but one founder. A third party archive names John Sillings as a second founder; not listed because no primary source confirms it.

technical_complexity.rationale: Events were run over standard video tools with shipped materials; the work was operations.

defensibility.rationale: Many vendors sold virtual team events in 2020 and nothing proprietary was needed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it; demand faded as offices reopened according to an unverified archive page.

market_need_then: Pandemic remote work from March 2020 created demand for virtual team activities; Y Combinator itself moved Winter 2020 Demo Day online.

branding.domain_note: Used miniexhibitions.com, the exact name as a .com

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; searches returned only generic art exhibition pages.

outcome_analysis: Mini Exhibitions was a two person New York company in the Winter 2020 batch selling virtual events for remote teams, and YC lists it as Inactive. No primary source gives the cause, funding or an end date; a single third party archive claims it wound down in late 2022 as pandemic remote work demand faded, which is recorded here only as an unverified lead, so no failure factor is asserted.
notes: The cause is not public beyond an unverified archive page (dead-startups-neon.vercel.app) that reports a quiet wind down in November 2022, YC-only funding of about 125,000 dollars, clients such as Amazon and Stripe, and John Sillings as co-founder; none of this is confirmed. YC's own page showed Active in one search snippet versus Inactive in the directory data. The company site did not resolve (miniexhibitions.com not reachable), treated as dead or unreachable. The dated competitor search returned only generic 2020 team building articles naming no rivals, so the list is empty.
